architectures.name: Direct creation (the show's gun)
architectures.description: The handheld device makes a new connection between here and a chosen remote place.

reqs.text: Create a connection to a chosen distant region on demand
reqs.basis: Classical spacetime: a theorem. Lorentzian (non-degenerate) topology change needs closed timelike curves (Geroch 1967); in Morse topology change the regions a new handle joins lie in the causal past of one event, so both mouths start there (local-creation lemma, D2 sec. 7.2, a corollary of Borde et al. 1999 and Dowker, Garcia & Surya 2000). Quantum nucleation: the one explicit wormhole construction (Horowitz, Marolf, Santos & Wang 2019) creates the mouths a finite distance apart, but that distance is set by a background (a cosmic string in anti-de Sitter space) that already spans the gap, and the rate e^(-2 dS) vanishes in the static limit. No known process puts a mouth where the device has had no prior causal reach.
reqs.assumptions: Theorem for classical or semiclassical spacetime without closed timelike curves, with topology change Lorentzian or through isolated Morse degeneracies. For quantum nucleation, an observation about every known construction, not a theorem.

reqs.text: Hold a macroscopic shortcut throat open
reqs.basis: QI audit: smooth throats excluded by 10^62 for any flare-out; the thin-band escape needs |rho| = 1.6e+64 J/m^3 (no known matter) under Ford & Roman's window, and a sub-Planckian band (3e-63 m) under the curvature-only window (Krasnikov 2003).
reqs.assumptions: Flat-space QIs applied with f = 0.01; free fields.

reqs.basis: All explicit models unstable (D2 sec. 6).
No theory supplies a mechanism.

architectures.name: Pre-existing connection (network terminal)
architectures.description: Linked mouths already exist; the device opens and steers a local mouth.

reqs.text: A macroscopic traversable shortcut exists already (natural or built)
reqs.basis: No natural mechanism; none detected (lensing searches give upper limits); a shortcut violates the achronal ANEC, conjectured to hold self-consistently.

reqs.text: It stays open with available matter
reqs.basis: As A2.
Ellis e-folds in 2.82 ns; feedback needs loop delay < 3.99 ns and NEC-violating actuation.
Tidal impulse ~ v w / r0 ~ 1 m/s at walking speed through smooth or thin-band throats.
Vertical pairs reach closed causal curves in 354 days; the network checker gives days to millennia; manageable by schedule.

Misner-Sharp sum rule (Visser, Kar & Dadhich 2003 eq. 8): a static spherical mouth lighter than r0 c^2/2G = 0.35 Jupiter masses contains negative energy of that size; otherwise it weighs as much as a black hole of the throat's size. For any shape, the Riemannian Penrose inequality (Huisken & Ilmanen 2001) still forces negative energy density somewhere outside a light mouth (D2 sec. 4.4).
reqs.assumptions: Time-symmetric or maximal slice; throat outermost from that end.

architectures.name: Distributed system
architectures.description: A facility creates throats locally, keeps them, and carries mouths at <= c; the handheld unit is a terminal.

reqs.basis: Classical: needs CTCs (Geroch) or degenerate (Morse) metrics; a single index-2 point makes a handle causally continuously (Dowker & Surya 1998; Dowker & Garcia 1998). Quantum: one explicit nucleation in anti-de Sitter space (Horowitz et al. 2019), rate e^(-2 dS), traversability argued rather than computed; no controllable rate.
As A2.
As B3.
As B4.
A launched mouth keeps margin 1 - (1 - 1/gamma)/beta; drift rates U/c^2 - v^2/2c^2.
As B6.

architectures.name: Mouth launcher (the video-game gun)
architectures.description: The device holds one mouth of a locally made pair and fires the other at a surface in line of sight.

reqs.text: Create a throat at the device
reqs.basis: As C1.
As A2.
As B3, plus acceleration loads.

reqs.text: Fire a mouth to the target
reqs.basis: Accelerating a mouth means pushing its exotic structure; its inertia is its ADM mass, zero for a massless mouth: no established dynamics.
Launch at beta leaves margin fraction 1 - (1 - sqrt(1-beta^2))/beta > 0.
As B6.

architectures.name: Polygonal flat-face portal
architectures.description: Visser's cut-and-paste portal: flat faces, exotic matter only on the rim strings; the best-behaved geometry for travellers.

reqs.basis: As C1.
QI forces rim core radius <= 5.6e-32 m (Planck scale): quantum-gravity regime. Krasnikov (2003) reaches the same Planck-thickness estimate for a smoothed portal.

Static circular rims exist as exact solutions (Gibbons & Volkov 2017; Feng, Lemos & Matzner 2021). Dynamics need a finite core: zero-thickness strings are not distributional sources (Geroch & Traschen 1987) and idealised conical worldsheets must be totally geodesic (Unruh et al. 1989; Boisseau, Charmousis & Linet 1997). No stability analysis of a rim exists.
Flat faces: no tides away from the rim.
Rim mass-energy -1.1 M_J per metre radius with zero Komar mass: what a hand would feel is not established.

architectures.name: Information portal
architectures.description: Scan, transmit at light speed, rebuild; plus a live two-way window.

reqs.text: Move the same matter through a shortcut
reqs.basis: Nothing moves; signals take at least the light time. Fails the portal definition by design.
Telepresence exists; delivery is ordinary transport.

architectures.name: Krasnikov tube / warp corridor
architectures.description: A corridor of modified spacetime laid at <= c, then fast for later travellers.

reqs.basis: Built at <= c along the route (Krasnikov 1998).

Everett & Roman (1997): QIs make the walls <~ 10^4 Planck lengths thick, and a tube 1 m long and 1 m wide needs ~10^16 galaxy masses of negative energy. Every Natario-class warp drive violates the WEC, and the NEC under plausible conditions (Santiago, Schuster & Visser 2022).
Two tubes can form closed timelike curves (Everett & Roman 1997); Krasnikov (1998) calls such devices 'square roots' of time machines.

architectures.name: Long wormhole (QFT-supported)
architectures.description: Traversable wormholes supported by quantum fields, longer than the outside path.

reqs.basis: Requires magnetically charged near-extremal black holes or a dark sector. The humanly traversable example has mouths of radius ~1.5e7 m (about 1e4 solar masses each, from M = r_e c^2/G), a throat ~3e3 light years long and ~1e4 years of outside travel time (Maldacena & Milekhin 2021).

Fails by definition: these constructions are computed to be slower than the outside route (Gao-Jafferis-Wall; Maldacena-Milekhin-Popov), which is what lets them respect the achronal ANEC; a shortcut version would need the AANEC violation of milestone M1.

milestones.question: Do quantum inequalities hold in curved spacetime with controlled error terms?
milestones.result_needed: QIs for curved backgrounds with explicit remainders in terms of curvature and sampling time.
milestones.counts_if: Bounds valid for sampling times up to a fixed fraction of the curvature radius.
milestones.method: Point-splitting and Hadamard-parametrix methods; null-smeared and worldline QIs.
milestones.progress: Remainder terms small at f ~ 0.01-0.1 for the geometries of D2 sec. 5.
milestones.terminates: Explicit states violating flat-space-type bounds at those scales.
milestones.unlocks: Turns the phase II QI audit from a method into theorems (M1, M3, M4 depend on it).

milestones.question: Can quantum fields coupled to gravity violate the achronal ANEC on macroscopic scales?
milestones.result_needed: A self-consistent semiclassical (or quantum-gravity) solution containing a macroscopic achronal ANEC violation, or a proof that none exists.
milestones.counts_if: Solution with throat >> l_P satisfying the semiclassical Einstein equation and known QIs.
milestones.method: Curved-space QI/ANEC proofs (null-projected and smeared QIs), holographic constructions, lattice QFT on curved backgrounds.
milestones.progress: Any controlled example of AANEC violation over a region larger than the curvature scale.
milestones.terminates: Proof of AANEC (or of a QI with Planck-suppressed loopholes) in curved spacetime.
milestones.unlocks: Holding open any shortcut throat (M3, M4).

milestones.question: Is there a physical, computable mechanism for topology change?
milestones.result_needed: Rates for handle nucleation in a theory of quantum gravity, and their dependence on controllable fields.
milestones.counts_if: Non-negligible rate for macroscopic or growable handles.
milestones.method: Euclidean instantons (Horowitz-Marolf-Santos-Wang type), causal-set or spin-foam sums with Morse-index weighting.
milestones.progress: A causally continuous (index-2) creation route with finite particle production and non-zero amplitude.
milestones.terminates: Topology change shown to require Planck curvature with exponentially small rates for any macroscopic seed.

milestones.question: Is there NEC-violating matter that can be concentrated into a 10^-21 m band at 10^64 J/m^3?
milestones.result_needed: A state of known fields reaching the thin-band requirement while obeying all QIs.
milestones.counts_if: Explicit state (e.g. squeezed or Casimir-type) with the required density and support.
milestones.method: QI optimisation over states; search for interacting-field QI violations.
milestones.progress: Any negative energy density above the free-field QI at the needed scale.
milestones.terminates: QIs proven for interacting fields at those densities.
milestones.unlocks: Thin-band throats (the only QI-compatible smooth-family escape).

milestones.question: Do negative-tension codimension-2 objects (|mu| = c^2/4G) exist as dynamical objects?
milestones.result_needed: A consistent theory with movable negative-tension strings at Planck thickness.
milestones.counts_if: Dynamical defects whose tension can be set and whose ends/corners can be supported.
milestones.method: String-theory defects, effective field theories of defects, QI analysis of conical excess.
milestones.terminates: Proof that negative-tension defects are always non-dynamical or ghost-like.

milestones.question: Is any traversable geometry stable against generic perturbations and traffic?
milestones.result_needed: A solution with no growing modes for all perturbations, including infalling matter.
milestones.counts_if: Spectral and nonlinear stability with physical matter.
milestones.method: Master equations (as in D2 sec. 6), time evolution, energy methods; parametric and feedback schemes.
milestones.progress: Stable example with matter satisfying QIs (or the matter of M3/M4).
milestones.terminates: General instability theorem for NEC-violating throats.

milestones.question: Can a mouth be moved and steered with known forces?
milestones.result_needed: Equations of motion of a mouth under applied stress-energy, including its exotic support.
milestones.counts_if: A mouth accelerated to v without destroying the throat.
milestones.method: Matched asymptotics / effective point-particle description of mouths; numerical relativity.
milestones.terminates: Inconsistency of mouth transport with QIs or stability.

milestones.question: Can chronology be managed operationally?
milestones.result_needed: Control laws keeping every cycle weight of the network positive with a safety margin.
milestones.counts_if: Schedules that bound all time shifts below the light-time margins.
milestones.method: The chronology checker (D3) plus vacuum-polarisation estimates near the margin.
milestones.terminates: Semiclassical instability at margins far larger than any achievable control.

milestones.question: Can a device-scale mouth be light?
milestones.result_needed: A mouth with ADM mass << r0 c^2/2G and its negative Misner-Sharp energy confined.
milestones.method: Misner-Sharp bookkeeping (D2 sec. 4) beyond spherical symmetry; the Penrose-inequality corollary of D2 sec. 4.4 gives existence of negative energy, not its amount.
milestones.terminates: A general quantitative theorem extending the sum rule.

milestones.question: Do natural traversable wormholes exist?
milestones.result_needed: A detection (lensing by negative-mass-like objects, shadows, echoes) or a mechanism that creates and keeps them.
milestones.counts_if: A confirmed object with a throat and no horizon.
milestones.method: Microlensing and strong-lensing searches; event-horizon imaging; gravitational-wave echoes.
milestones.terminates: Not a stopping criterion: absence proves little.
milestones.still_unsolved: Holding open is still needed if it must be enlarged.

milestones.question: Does the 'heavy or negative' mass rule hold for general (dynamical) mouths?
milestones.result_needed: A Penrose-type inequality for traversable throats in general initial data.
milestones.counts_if: Bound M >= sqrt(A/16 pi) unless the dominant energy condition fails somewhere.
milestones.method: Spacetime Penrose inequality methods; marginally outer trapped surfaces.
milestones.progress: Already holds on time-symmetric and maximal slices, which include circular stationary rotating mouths (Huisken & Ilmanen 2001, applied in D2 sec. 4.4).
milestones.terminates: A light traversable mouth whose matter obeys the dominant energy condition. (With the weak energy condition alone, counterexamples to Penrose-type inequalities exist: Jaracz 2023.)
milestones.unlocks: Settles whether a handheld mouth must carry negative energy (M8).
